description:
Donations are tax deductible and we need your support to continue our work. Text-to-donate, text VSRF to 53555.Show more Join us Thursday, January 8, 2026, for our first episode of VSRF Live in the new year! We’ll be joined by Nic Hulscher, a public-health researcher and data analyst known for his rigorous examination of COVID-era assumptions, testing methodologies, and long-term health outcomes that continue to shape policy today.
At the heart of this conversation is a simple but essential question: Did the data ever justify the decisions made in the name of public health?
Topics we’ll explore include:
🔹 PCR Testing & Case Counts
New analyses suggest that a substantial share of PCR-positive “COVID-19 cases” may not have represented active or clinically meaningful infections. We’ll examine how cycle thresholds, mass testing of asymptomatic populations, and evolving case definitions influenced public perception—and whether policy decisions were driven by flawed interpretations of the data.
🔹 Lockdowns, Mandates & Public Policy
Were sweeping restrictions supported by robust evidence? We’ll discuss how testing practices, institutional incentives, and data modeling may have shaped public-policy decisions that profoundly altered daily life, education, and healthcare access worldwide.
🔹 Vitamin D, Cancer & Preventive Health
A growing body of research points to vitamin D status as a potentially significant factor in cancer risk reduction and immune health. Why has this remained largely absent from mainstream public-health guidance, and what does the evidence actually show?
🔹 Vaccinated vs. Unvaccinated Health Outcomes
Across multiple observational studies comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated children, consistent patterns have emerged showing higher rates of chronic illness and neurodevelopmental diagnoses in vaccinated groups. We’ll discuss the findings, their limitations, and why these results remain so contentious—and so often dismissed.
🔹 Amyloid Microclots & Spike-Related Pathology
Recent peer-reviewed research has identified fibrinolysis-resistant amyloid microclots in vaccinated individuals, including those classified as “healthy controls.” We’ll break down what’s been observed, what remains unknown, and the potential implications for long-term vascular health.
🔹 Maternal Exposure & Infant Health
Emerging data raise serious questions about in-utero exposure to mRNA products and possible downstream effects in infants. What evidence exists so far, and what studies should be urgently pursued?
At its core, this conversation is about science, evidence, and accountability.
If the data are sound, they should withstand scrutiny. If they’re not, the public deserves transparency, no matter how uncomfortable the conclusions may be.
Join us on Thursday, January 8, 2026, as VSRF Live ushers in the new year with an in-depth, evidence-based discussion that challenges assumptions and follows the data wherever it leads. Show less
